Verified by Debora Aust on November 14, 2023 Debora is a relocation expert at DARE Consulting. She helps skilled immigrants move to Germany since 2015. Debora is a relocation expert at DARE Consulting. She helps skilled immigrants move to Germany since 2015. The EU Blue Card ( Blaue Karte) is a residence permit for skilled workers. With a Blue Card, you can… Live and work anywhere in Germany Bring your family to Germany Visit other Schengen countries without a visa Become a permanent resident after 21 to 27 months Become a citizen after 5 years This guide explains how to apply for a Blue Card in Berlin or in your home country.

If you are not a citizen of the EU, EEA or Switzerland, you need a residence permit to live in Germany. The Blue Card is a type of residence permit. If you are a permanent resident, you don’t need a Blue Card. You can already work anywhere. Who needs a residence permit?

To get a Blue Card, you need… A guaranteed job offer in Germany You must find a job before you apply for the Blue Card. The job must have… A German employer You must work for a German employer, or an employer with an office in Germany. It can be a remote job. You must be an employee, not a freelancer. A high salary Your salary must be over € 50,700 per year (before taxes, without bonuses). If your job is in the list of shortage occupations, your salary must be over € 45,934 per year. If you graduated less than 3 years ago, your salary must be over € 45,934 per year. Your salary must cover the cost of living for you and your family. A long term contract Your job contract must be for at least 6 months. A German employer You must work for a German employer, or an employer with an office in Germany. It can be a remote job. You must be an employee, not a freelancer. A high salary Your salary must be over € 50,700 per year (before taxes, without bonuses). If your job is in the list of shortage occupations, your salary must be over € 45,934 per year. If you graduated less than 3 years ago, your salary must be over € 45,934 per year. Your salary must cover the cost of living for you and your family. A long term contract Your job contract must be for at least 6 months. Qualifications for this job You must know how to do your job. For example, to get a programming job, you must know how to program. Permission to do this job You must have all the permits and special qualifications needed for the job. For example, doctors, engineers and lawyers need special qualifications. – Find the requirements for your job A university degree Your university degree must be recognised in Germany. Use Anabin to see if your university and degree are recognised. – How to use Anabin You do not need a university degree if… You are an IT specialist and you have at least 3 years of experience and your salary is over € 45,934 per year You do not need to speak German to get a Blue Card. If you can’t get a Blue Card, there are other residence permits that let you work in Germany. Blue Card alternatives

You can apply for a Blue Card before or after you move to Germany. To apply after moving to Germany, you must… Come to Germany Apply for a Blue Card at your local Ausländerbehörde. In Berlin, you must apply online. If you don’t live in Berlin, find your local Ausländerbehörde and follow their instructions. Get your Blue Card Start working You can apply in Germany if… You are a citizen of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco or San Marino or you already have a German residence permit, and you want to change it or renew it or you have a Blue Card from another EU country or you have an EU Permanent Residence in another country or you have an opportunity card or you have a job seeker visa or you have a National Visa that you must convert to a Blue Card. If you can’t apply in Germany, you must apply in your home country. Usually, you can’t start working before you get your Blue Card. You might wait 2 to 5 months with no income. To get a Blue Card faster, use the Business Immigration Service. It’s cheaper and safer if you apply in your home country, then come to Germany when you have permission to work. If you need help, an immigration lawyer or a relocation consultant can take care of everything. It costs € 500 to € 2,000. Your employer might pay for it, or hire someone to help you.

title: 1. Come to Germany
text: Come to Germany and look for a job. If you have a National Visa or residence permit If your current visa or residence permit expires after you applied for the Blue Card, you don’t need to leave Germany. It stays valid until you get your Blue Card. If you are a citizen of Australia, Canada, Israel, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, the United Kingdom, the United States, Andorra, Brazil, El Salvador, Honduras, Monaco or San Marino You can come to Germany without a visa. You can stay 90 days in Germany without a residence permit. You can look for a job, and apply for the Blue Card in Germany. You can’t work before you get your Blue Card. If you have a Blue Card from another EU country You can come to Germany without a visa. If you have your Blue Card since at least 12 months, you can already start working in Germany. When you arrive in Germany, you have 1 month to convert your Blue Card to a German one at the Ausländerbehörde. If you have an opportunity card You can come to Germany and look for a job. You can work 20 hours per week. To work full time, you must switch to a Blue Card or a work visa. If you have a job seeker visa You can already start working. You don’t need to wait for your Blue Card. If you have a Schengen visa Schengen visas are for tourism, not immigration. Usually, if you enter Germany with a Schengen visa, you can’t apply for a Blue Card in Germany. Your application will be rejected. You must apply in your home country. If these options don’t apply to you, you must apply for the Blue Card in your home country.

title: 2. Find a job
text: You must find a job before you apply for the Blue Card. Your job offer must meet the Blue Card requirements. How to find a job

title: 3. Prepare your application
text: Before you apply for the Blue Card… Find a place to live It’s really hard to find an apartment. Start looking as soon as you can. You must be allowed to register your address. Your landlord must give you a tenancy confirmation. If you can’t get a tenancy confirmation, you might not get a Blue Card. Your rent must be affordable. Your total cost of living must be less than your net income. Your apartment must be big enough. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child. You must be allowed to register your address. Your landlord must give you a tenancy confirmation. If you can’t get a tenancy confirmation, you might not get a Blue Card. Your rent must be affordable. Your total cost of living must be less than your net income. Your apartment must be big enough. You need 9 m² per adult, and 6 m² per child. Get health insurance You need valid health insurance. Ask my insurance expert to help you choose the correct health insurance. Prepare the required documents If you bring your family to Germany, you can apply for their family reunion visa at the same time. You must prepare their documents too. While you wait for your Ausländerbehörde appointment, you should also… Register your address ( Anmeldung) The Anmeldung is very important. When you register your address, you get a tax ID and a registration certificate. If you don’t do your Anmeldung, they might reject your application. Open a bank account You need it to pay your rent, pay your Blue Card application fee, and get paid by your employer. You can choose a bank from any EU country.

title: 4. Apply for the Blue Card online
text: You must apply for the Blue Card online. You do not need an Ausländerbehörde appointment. It takes 15 minutes. Apply for the Blue Card It costs € 100. It’s cheaper for Turkish citizens. You can pay with Visa, Mastercard or PayPal. You can’t pay with cash or Girocard. The fee is tax-deductible, so keep the receipt. If you have too many documents, merge them or make them smaller. After you pay and send your application, you can download a PDF. This is your proof of application. Save it for later. You can also apply through the Business Immigration Service. It’s free, and it’s usually much faster. Your employer must do it for you.

title: 5. Wait
text: The Ausländerbehörde will process your application. It takes 2 to 5 months. You must wait for their response. There is no way to track your application. If you wait more than 3 months, you can sue the Ausländerbehörde. While you wait, your current National Visa or residence permit might expire. It’s extended until the Ausländerbehörde processes your application. If your visa or residence permit expires If you have an opportunity card, you can work 20 hours per week while you wait for your Blue Card. What happens while you wait

title: 6. Go to your appointment
text: A few weeks later, the Ausländerbehörde will give you an appointment date by email. If you get an appointment, you are almost guaranteed to get your Blue Card. Follow the instructions in the email. You might need to send extra documents, or bring them to your appointment. What happens during your appointment If your Blue Card is approved, you will get a second appointment to pick up your plastic residence card. While you wait, you can start working. You will get a document that confirms this.

title: 7. Get your Blue Card
text: Go to your second Ausländerbehörde appointment and pick up your Blue Card. Your new Blue Card is valid for up to 4 years. If you have a limited work contract, your Blue Card is valid for a shorter time. For example, if you have a 2 year work contract, your Blue Card is valid for 2 years + 3 months. How to pick up your Blue Card Tell us how long it took to apply for a residence permit in Berlin. This tool requires JavaScript to work.

section: How to apply in your country
text: You can also apply for a Blue Card in your country, then move to Germany. This is cheaper and safer, because when you arrive in Germany, you can already start working. You don’t need to wait in Germany without an income. You must find a job before you apply. Your job offer must meet the Blue Card requirements. If you don’t have a job offer, you can get an opportunity card, come to Germany, find a job, then apply for a Blue Card in Germany. To get a Blue Card faster, use the fast-track procedure ( Beschleunigtes Verfahren). It costs € 411. How to apply in your country

These are the required documents in Berlin. If you apply elsewhere, they require different documents. Check the website of the Ausländerbehörde, embassy or consulate where you apply. – Find your embassy or consulate Passport When you apply online, include a colour scan of your passport. When you go to your appointment, bring your original passport. You get it back during the appointment; they do not keep it. QR code for biometric pictures (35 × 45 mm) Printed passport photos are not allowed. Only QR codes are accepted. See how to get biometric pictures. Job contract or job offer Bring the original, not a copy. Job description form ( Erklärung zum Beschäftigungsverhältnis) Your employer should fill this form and sign it. Download the form here or on Berlin.de. Proof of health insurance You need valid health insurance. Travel health insurance is not accepted. Ask my insurance expert to help you choose health insurance for your Blue Card. Health insurance card Show both sides of the card. proof of public health insurance Get a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB V from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. proof of private health insurance Bring your insurance contract, a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. Health insurance card Show both sides of the card. proof of public health insurance Get a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 175 SGB V from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. proof of private health insurance Bring your insurance contract, a Mitgliedsbescheinigung nach § 257 SGB V, and bank statements that show health insurance payments. Get these documents from your health insurer or your health insurance broker. Proof of housing You need a place to live where you can register your address. If you apply in Berlin, your home address must be in Berlin. Lease Bring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child). You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, a WG or a sublet. and tenancy confirmation ( Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. You might not get a Blue Card without it. and registration certificate ( Anmeldebestätigung) You must register your address to get this document. If you don’t have it, your lease and tenancy confirmation are sometimes enough. At least bring proof that you have a Bürgeramt appointment. Lease Bring the original, not a copy. It must show the size of your apartment. Your apartment must be big enough (9 m² per adult, 6 m² per child). You must make enough money to pay your rent. It can be a temporary lease, a WG or a sublet. and tenancy confirmation ( Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) Some temporary apartments and sublets don’t give you this document. You might not get a Blue Card without it. and registration certificate ( Anmeldebestätigung) You must register your address to get this document. If you don’t have it, your lease and tenancy confirmation are sometimes enough. At least bring proof that you have a Bürgeramt appointment. University degree If you are an IT specialist with at least 3 years of experience, you don’t need a degree. Statement of comparability ( Zeugnisbewertung) If your university degree is not recognised in Germany, you must get a statement of comparability ( Zeugnisbewertung) from the ZAB. If you are an IT specialist with at least 3 years of experience, you don’t need this. – More information Occupation practice permit ( Berufsausübungserlaubnis) If you need specific qualifications to do your job, bring all the required diplomas and permits. For example, doctors, engineers and tax advisors need specific qualifications. Use the recognition finder to know if you need specific qualifications. Translations If your documents are not in German, bring translations. For certificates and official documents, bring certified translations. They sometimes accept untranslated documents, but don’t take the risk. Get translations from Red Tape Translation or Lingoking. Use PDF files or photos. Don’t use Word documents or other file formats. Put dates on all your documents.

section: After you get your Blue Card
title: Give feedback
text: Tell me how long it took to get your Blue Card. Your feedback helps thousands of people plan their application. Tell us how long it took to apply for a residence permit in Berlin. This tool requires JavaScript to work.

section: After you get your Blue Card
title: Renew your Blue Card
text: Your Blue Card is valid for up to 4 years. In Berlin, you must renew it around 6 weeks before it expires, not sooner. To renew your Blue Card, you must use the same form that you used to apply for your Blue Card, or use the contact form. You can also apply for permanent residence after 27 months. If you speak B1 German, you can get it after 21 months.

section: After you get your Blue Card
title: If you change or lose your job
text: If you change jobs, always tell the Ausländerbehörde. You might need their permission to work for a different employer. If you lose your job, your Blue Card stays valid. Tell the Ausländerbehörde as soon as you can. In Berlin, they give you 6 to 12 months to find another job. You might get unemployment benefits. What happens to your Blue Card How unemployment benefits work

section: After you get your Blue Card
title: Travel with a Blue Card
text: Your Blue Card lets you visit other Schengen area countries for up to 90 days without a visa. You can travel outside of Germany for up to 12 months. If you travel longer, your Blue Card expires. Your Blue Card lets you live anywhere in Germany, not just in the city where you applied. Travel with a residence permit

section: After you get your Blue Card
title: Self-employment with a Blue Card
text: Your Blue Card might allow part-time self-employment. In Berlin, Blue Cards usually allow self-employment. Check your Zusatzblatt. Check your work contract too. You might need to tell your employer about your self-employment. Your employer might forbid self-employment if it competes with their business. For example, don’t start a marketing agency while you work for another marketing agency. They can’t forbid all self-employment without a reason. To become self-employed full time, apply for a freelance visa, permanent residence or citizenship.

section: After you get your Blue Card
title: Apply for permanent residence
text: If you have a Blue Card, you qualify for permanent residence after 27 months. If you speak B1 German, you qualify after 21 months. Permanent residence is better than a Blue Card, because it’s not tied to your job. How to apply for permanent residence

An immigration lawyer or a relocation consultant can answer your questions. Some organisations can also help you for free. Your employer might offer help.
